harness: structural - each case is checked against the skill's own rules, not against a model run

cases.prompt: Our Meta leads doubled last month but revenue did not move. Here is the funnel by stage and our contribution margin per order.
expect_must: lays the funnel out stage by stage with a source per stage
computes the rupee value of a 20% improvement at each stage before naming the constraint
checks lead qualification and the offer before recommending more traffic
names one experiment with a pre-registered metric, sample and kill rule
expect_must_not: recommend increasing spend as the first action
quote a benchmark from another market as if it were this business's data

cases.prompt: Growth has plateaued. What should we do?
expect_must: asks for the funnel by stage, contribution margin, spend by channel and what has been tried
offers a diagnosis checklist the user can fill in from exports
states which parts cannot be answered without the numbers
expect_must_not: recommend a channel without the funnel
assume an industry, a price point or a margin

cases.prompt: Pull our GA4 numbers for October and tell me which channel won.
expect_must: states whether an analytics connector exists in this session and does not claim to have read GA4
asks for the export or the sheet, and says which export answers the question
names the reconciliation needed: platform versus analytics versus gateway
expect_must_not: invent traffic, conversion or channel figures
declare a winning channel from nothing

cases.prompt: Set up our Diwali Meta campaigns, structure the ad sets and pace the budget so we spend 3 lakh in three weeks.
cases.expect_owner: growth-marketer scopes the test; performance-ads-buyer builds and paces the campaign
expect_must: routes campaign build, structure and pacing to performance-ads-buyer
keeps the part it owns: the hypothesis, the metric, the spend ceiling justified by payback
states that spend requires explicit approval and that it will not launch anything
expect_must_not: build ad sets and budgets itself
commit spend on the founder's behalf

cases.prompt: 60% of buyers never order again. Should we add Google Shopping?
cases.expect_owner: growth-marketer diagnoses; retention work hands to support-agent and the product side
expect_must: names retention as the constraint and shows why a new channel makes every CAC look worse
computes the effect of repeat rate on allowable CAC
hands the post-purchase and reorder sequence to support-agent or email-marketer, and the product experience to product-manager
offers a reorder experiment as the next test instead of a new channel
expect_must_not: recommend adding a channel to compensate for churn
promise a repeat-rate improvement without a mechanism
